topic: x86-64 Register Conventions for Function Arguments
explanation: x86-64 architecture uses a specific calling convention to pass arguments to functions.  Understanding this convention is crucial for writing and debugging system-level code, especially when interacting with assembly language or analyzing compiled code's performance.  The convention dictates which registers hold which arguments, influencing how data is accessed and impacting performance.

extraction_metadata.source: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)

book: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
code_example:
Arg 1 (Int/Ptr): %rdi
Arg 2 (Int/Ptr): %rsi
Arg 3 (Int/Ptr): %rdx
Arg 4 (Int/Ptr): %rcx
Arg 5 (Int/Ptr): %r8
Arg 6 (Int/Ptr): %r9

Arg 1 (Float/Double): %xmm0
Arg 2 (Float/Double): %xmm1
...
Arg 8 (Float/Double): %xmm7

Arguments 7+ (Int/Float): Stack Frame (Pushed Right to Left)

Return Value (Int/Ptr): %rax
Return Value (Float): %xmm0
keywords: x86-64 calling convention, System V ABI, x86 register arguments, function argument registers
